title: Merge Sorted Array
prompt: You are given two integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, sorted in non-decreasing order, along with integers `m` and `n` representing the number of valid elements in `nums1` and `nums2` respectively. `nums1` has a length of `m + n`, where the last `n` slots are `0` and should be ignored, since they exist only to leave room for `nums2`. Merge `nums2` into `nums1` in place so that the result is a single sorted array.
hints: Merging from the front requires shifting elements right repeatedly — that's O(m*n) in the worst case. Is there a direction that avoids shifting?
nums1 has empty space at the END, not the beginning. What if you filled the array back-to-front instead?

Use three pointers: one at the last valid element of nums1, one at the last element of nums2, and one at the very last slot of nums1. Always place the larger of the two candidates at the write pointer and move it left.

solution.approach: Since nums1 has trailing empty slots exactly sized to fit nums2, fill the array from the back instead of the front. Compare the last unmerged elements of nums1 and nums2, place the larger at the current end position, and move that source pointer and the write pointer left. This avoids ever shifting already-placed elements, since we always write into a slot that hasn't been used yet, giving a single O(m+n) pass with no extra space.
